name: How to Fish Beginner Guide: Tips & Early Progression
description: Start How to Fish with beginner fishing controls, Lighthouse quests, selling, the Crab Fishing Rod, boat key, Radar and early weapon priorities.
imageAlt: Official How to Fish gameplay screenshot showing a player fishing beside the starter boat

sections.heading: Your first objective
paragraphs: How to Fish is a physics-driven fishing adventure, not a traditional real-world fishing simulator. Your opening loop is simple: catch a creature, defeat it, sell it, then spend the money on stronger equipment and boat upgrades.

For the quickest early progression, complete the Lighthouse dialogue loop first: use the Crab Fishing Rod, keep the Empty Beer Can for Spider Crab, return the quest result for the boat key, then buy the Radar before heading to Forest Island.
bullets: Talk to nearby characters before leaving an island.
The opening rods have internal default pools; there is no reusable inventory item named Free Lure.
Buy or equip a named bait only when its catch table or quest calls for it.

sections.heading: Opening tutorial actions
paragraphs: The tutorial begins with a Clam on the Lighthouse ground. Pick it up with the interact control, then throw a sellable catch into the shopkeeper's mouth to receive money. Buy the Crab-Fishing Rod from the opening shop before trying the shoreline pools.
bullets: Eat a creature when you need to restore hunger.
Use Inspect to check an item's current value before selling it.
Open the caught-creature view with Tab when you need to check collection progress.

sections.heading: Landing a catch
paragraphs: Cast into visible water and pay attention to the pull of the line. When the catch reaches the boat, fishing turns into combat. The game rewards creative kills, so positioning the creature before firing can be worth the effort.
bullets: Create space before using explosives.
Use the weapon you can land consistently, then experiment with trick shots.
A failed catch usually costs time, so restock before a longer trip.

sections.heading: Spend money in the right order
paragraphs: A reliable weapon and a boat engine upgrade give the strongest early quality-of-life improvement. Attachments become more valuable once you know which weapon you actually enjoy using.
bullets: Reliability first: weapon, ammunition and lure access.
Mobility second: the engine shortens return trips.
Specialization last: attachments and completion-focused purchases.

sections.heading: When to move on
paragraphs: Progression is tied to island objectives, quests and boss encounters. If the next route is unclear, return to the current island, talk to every marked character and check whether you still need a boss-specific lure.

faq.question: Is How to Fish single-player?
faq.answer: Yes. The game supports single-player, and Patch 1.0.4 raised online co-op lobby support to up to eight players.

faq.question: Do I need to keep every fish?
faq.answer: No. Selling catches is a core part of progression; keep only what a current quest or lure chain requires.

faq.question: Why will a fish not bite?
faq.answer: The usual causes are the wrong island, the wrong lure, or a prerequisite encounter that has not been completed.

name: How to Fish Walkthrough: All Islands, Bosses & Quests
description: Complete the How to Fish walkthrough from Lighthouse to Volcano with every island unlock, boss trigger, bait requirement, trophy and NPC hand-in.
imageAlt: Official How to Fish screenshot of the starting island route

sections.heading: Lighthouse opening
paragraphs: Start the complete How to Fish island walkthrough at Lighthouse: learn the catch-kill-sell loop, complete the beer-related objective and use the locally available bait chain to reach the Spider Crab encounter. Its return hand-in gives the boat key and opens the route toward Forest Island.
bullets: Catch basic shoreline creatures.
Finish nearby NPC requests.
Prepare the Empty Beer Can path for Spider Crab.

sections.heading: Forest Island
paragraphs: Bring three ground leeches to the lady by the lake, use Leech Bait for Giant Piranha and return its trophy for the next coordinates. The $40 Beginner Boss Lure encounters are optional.
bullets: Clear the default Fishing Rod pool and the nine-target Beginner Lure pool.
Secure Leech Bait before Giant Piranha.
Return the named trophy—not generic meat.

sections.heading: Desert Island
paragraphs: Catch an eligible endangered creature with the $15 Standard Lure and trade it to the tourist for a Carrot; Needlefish and Seahorse are confirmed options. Blue Shark uses the $280 Standard Boss Lure and unlocks the grill; Pufferfish uses the Carrot and unlocks Rocks Island.
bullets: Do Blue Shark for the 1.5x cooking route.
Keep the Carrot for Pufferfish.
Return the Pufferfish fin.

sections.heading: Rocks Island
paragraphs: Buy the $1,200 Professional Boss Lure for Tuna, keep the body, then place it on the ground for Albatross. Return the bird's head for Volcano coordinates.
bullets: Clear the $50 Professional Lure pool.
Do not sell or cook Tuna.
Use a ranged weapon for Albatross.

sections.heading: Volcano Island
paragraphs: Use the $500 Scientific Lure for regular entries. The $5,800 Goblin Shark lure is optional; the story follows Bowhead Whale into the mutated final encounter.
bullets: Check Tab before buying the optional boss lure.
Keep Bowhead Whale for the next trigger.
Finish the mutated phase and take the final transport.

faq.question: How many islands are in the launch route?
faq.answer: Launch guides and achievement progression consistently point to five major island stages.

faq.question: Can I play the route in co-op?
faq.answer: Yes. Patch 1.0.4 raised online co-op lobby support to up to eight players.

name: Island Progression & Unlock Order
description: The five-island progression order, what to finish before leaving, and which lure tiers matter next.
imageAlt: Official gameplay screenshot showing an island camp near a lighthouse

sections.heading: Recommended order
bullets: 1. Lighthouse — Spider Crab trophy, boat key and $10 Radar.
2. Forest Island — three leeches, Leech Bait and Giant Piranha trophy.
3. Desert Island — endangered-creature trade, Carrot and Pufferfish fin.
4. Rocks Island — $1,200 Tuna, Albatross and bird-head hand-in.
5. Volcano Island — military route and the two-stage whale ending.

sections.heading: Radar markers
paragraphs: The four destinations appear as green, yellow, red and pink dots. A new marker appears only after the named story trophy is handed back to the current quest giver.

faq.question: Why is the next island missing from my Radar?
faq.answer: Confirm the story boss dropped the named trophy and return it to the quest giver. The kill alone does not add the marker.

name: Fast Money Guide
description: Earn efficiently without pretending fish have one fixed sale value: route planning, kill score and low downtime matter.
imageAlt: Official How to Fish gameplay screenshot showing a gold weapon during combat

sections.heading: Best raw catch
paragraphs: Superdwarf Fish has a $1,700 raw base value, ahead of Anglerfish and Stonefish at $1,500. Those are starting values, not guaranteed final sale prices.
bullets: Scientific Lure costs $500.
Cook to about 1.5x, then remove the item before it burns.
Stack Killscore before cooking because the two systems are separate.

sections.heading: Killscore and cooking
bullets: 360: 1.5x; headshot and last bullet: 1.25x each.
No scope: 1.2x; point blank: 1.1x.
Cooking peaks at about 1.5x and a burnt-black item drops to zero value.

sections.heading: The $100,000 achievement
paragraphs: No ordinary raw fish reaches $100,000. Build a valuable item with Killscore and cooking, then use the roulette green payout. Green occupies one pocket in 37, so treat the item as expendable.

faq.question: Which creature has the highest raw base value?
faq.answer: Superdwarf Fish has the highest raw base value in the launch creature list at $1,700.

faq.question: Does a stylish kill pay more?
faq.answer: Yes. Killscore multiplies the item value and stacks separately with cooking.

name: Best Weapons & Upgrade Priorities
description: Choose weapons by consistency, range and encounter type, then match upgrades to the fights you are preparing for.
imageAlt: Official gameplay screenshot beside the How to Kill weapon shop

sections.heading: Best all-round approach
paragraphs: The pistol is a safe early tool, the shotgun is forgiving at close range, and the sniper rifle supports distance and trick-shot play. Explosives are powerful but punish cramped positioning.
bullets: Early game: choose a firearm you can afford to keep supplied.
Bosses: value burst damage and room to dodge.
Trick shots: use precise weapons after you understand the creature's movement.

sections.heading: Attachment priority
paragraphs: Attachments are strongest when they solve a real problem—accuracy, reload rhythm or engagement range. The official Fully equipped achievement confirms that one weapon can carry all attachment slots.

sections.heading: Do not ignore the boat
paragraphs: The engine is not a weapon, but faster travel improves every farming and quest route. The I am speed achievement confirms a highest engine tier.

faq.question: What is the single best weapon?
faq.answer: There is no universal best weapon. Encounter range and your ability to land shots matter more than a single tier list.

name: Rare Drip Fish Guide
description: Learn how Drip creatures work, plan a repeatable island sweep and finish the rare-variant achievements.
imageAlt: Official How to Fish gameplay screenshot of a player fishing near a tropical island

sections.heading: What Drip means
paragraphs: Drip is the game's rare-variant layer. Killing your first Drip creature unlocks Drip, while finding every Drip creature is required for Fishipedia.
bullets: Confirm the normal species and lure first.
Run a short repeatable route with low travel time.
Expect rarity; do not change bait after every failed attempt.
Use the blank Tab encyclopedia entries as your cleanup list.

sections.heading: What the game does not show
paragraphs: How to Fish does not display a spawn-rate percentage, luck formula or universal best time of day for Drip variants. Spend your time on short repeatable routes instead of chasing an unshown timer.

faq.question: Do Drip variants sell for more?
faq.answer: The game treats them as rare variants but does not show a fixed value multiplier. Inspect the catch before selling if you are farming money.

faq.question: Is there a Drip achievement?
faq.answer: Yes. Drip covers the first rare-variant kill, and Fishipedia requires every Drip creature.

name: 100% Completion Checklist
description: A compact route through the full catch directory, 28 achievements, quests, gear and final encounters.
imageAlt: Official gameplay screenshot with characters, a grill and a seagull encounter

sections.heading: Core completion blocks
bullets: Finish the five-island story route.
Find and kill every base creature needed for Collector.
Find and kill every Drip variant for Fishipedia.
Complete the named NPC quest achievements.
Buy the best engine and fully equip one weapon.
Clean up trick-shot, roulette and challenge achievements.

sections.heading: Missable-looking tasks
paragraphs: Most launch goals appear suitable for cleanup, but keep a save-state mindset around quest items and boss lures. Finish a local NPC chain before leaving and avoid consuming or selling an explicitly requested target.

sections.heading: Speedrun achievement
paragraphs: Bean asks for a finish within one hour. Attempt it after a normal completion run, when island routes and purchase priorities are familiar.

faq.question: How many Steam achievements are there?
faq.answer: The official Steam statistics page lists 28 achievements for the launch build.

name: Where to Find Leeches
description: A focused route for the leech-related progression item, with the distinction between a creature and a quest pickup.
imageAlt: Official gameplay screenshot showing a player fishing beside an island

sections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: Pick up three leeches from the Forest Island ground and bring them to the lady by the lake. She returns Leech Bait, the one-use bait for the Giant Piranha story boss.
bullets: Leeches are ground pickups, not rod catches.
Search grass, paths and shoreline ground around the quest area.
Confirm Leech Bait is in the inventory before casting.

sections.heading: If too few spawn
paragraphs: Revisit the lady's dialogue, sweep the island once more, then reload the area. Do not switch fishing lures—the missing object is on land.

faq.question: How many leeches do I need?
faq.answer: Three ground-spawned leeches are required to receive Leech Bait.
